title: Controlled Sparsity via Constrained Optimization or: How I Learned to Stop Tuning Penalties and Love Constraints
authors: Jose Gallego-Posada, Juan Ramirez, Akram Erraqabi, Yoshua Bengio, Simon Lacoste-Julien
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2022), Vol. 35
conclusions: Reformulates L0-norm sparsity targets (from Louizos et al.'s stochastic-gate penalty) as hard constraints (g(phi_g) <= epsilon_g) rather than additive penalties, solved via a Lagrangian primal-dual (GDA) scheme.

Empirically shows the penalized approach is brittle: the achieved density is insensitive to the penalty coefficient lambda_pen over many orders of magnitude, then changes abruptly (Fig. 1, Fig. 4) -- i.e. fixed-penalty tuning is unreliable for hitting a target sparsity.

The constrained approach reliably and directly achieves the desired target density across MLP/LeNet5/MNIST, ResNet18/WideResNet-28-10 on CIFAR-10/100/TinyImageNet, and ResNet50 on ImageNet, with no loss (often a gain) in predictive performance vs the penalized baseline.

Introduces a 'dual restart' heuristic: zero the Lagrange multiplier once its constraint is satisfied, rather than letting violation history accumulate, to prevent excessive post-satisfaction over-regularization (directly analogous to TraLO's own reset-at-satisfaction mechanism).
Reports that constraint dynamics stabilize quickly and do not oscillate badly in practice, despite the non-convex-concave min-max game lacking guaranteed saddle points.
Scales the constrained-Lagrangian approach to dozens of simultaneous per-layer constraints (48 for ResNet50), which the penalized method cannot tune tractably.
